findings.title: Denial cache key does not distinguish identity types
findings.body: The key uses `UserUID` but not `IdentityType`. For example, `anonymous:0` and `render:0` both produce the UID `0`; a cached denial for an anonymous dashboard read can therefore make a renderer check for the same resource return denied before the renderer’s wildcard read permission is evaluated. The reverse can also deny an anonymous user who has permission. Include the identity type in the denial key to prevent one identity’s decision from affecting another.

findings.title: Denial key can collide for different resource and folder pairs
findings.body: The key concatenates `name` and `parent` with an unescaped underscore. Since dashboard and folder UIDs can contain underscores, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key. A denial for the first check then short-circuits the second check even if that resource is allowed, for up to the cache TTL. Encode the components unambiguously, such as with length prefixes.
